part: independent audit script for the existing AB01/d10 pilot_v2 output
summary: The audit script is accepted (b3278c87...) and unchanged. Round 3 asked for wording fixes only (R3-1 to R3-3). The changes are confined to builder strings, one figure's marks and labels, and this handoff. No new data was read: the builder re-reads the same figure records as before, and the census is unchanged.
not_changed: backlog.json/html, AGENTS.md, guarded_launcher.py, producer modules, the reviewer's tests/test_audit_um21_tread_pilot_verify.py, converted_datasets/ and source folders.

design.independence: No import of extend_umich_tread_source, reconvert_umich_*, reconvert_recording or any contributor_tools module. An AST test pins imports to the stdlib plus numpy/h5py/pyarrow. The script also lists sys.modules at exit and fails the report if a producer or contributor_tools module was loaded. Resampling evaluates the exact rational position k*(n-1)/149. A sample that lands on a source frame takes that frame's value. A sample between frames takes the linear blend of the two, and is NaN if either neighbour is non-finite. Velocities use their own finite difference: one-sided at the ends, central inside. Neither np.interp nor np.gradient is used.
design.side_and_events: Pairs come from consecutive LHS (left) and RHS (right) heel strikes in the source. Parquet observations are matched by identity, not by row order. Ipsi and contra columns must equal the claimed leg's and the other leg's source channels. The report counts observations where the two legs' source windows differ, which is what makes the side check discriminating, and pairs whose frames occur on both sides.
design.clock: Basis is the README (R01 Dataset README.pdf): joint channels at 100 Hz, forceplates at 1000 Hz, HS and StrideTime in 100 Hz frames. Checks: StrideTime == diff(HS) exactly; forceplate length == 10 x joint length; HS inside the joint frames; median exported stride within 0.7-2.0 s (a x10 clock error falls outside); source_start/end_time_s = (frame-1)/100; time_s[k] = k*(end-start)/(149*100); phase_ipsi has 0 and 100 exactly and 150 equal steps; exactly 150 contiguous rows per observation.
design.values: Checks every source component in source_columns.json against the source (84 expected). Each column name must follow from its mapping entry, and each unit must match the README unit for its group. The prior columns are checked two ways: bit for bit against the base phase.parquet, and against the documented base recipe from source (pelvis = RPelvisAngles; thigh = pelvis + hip; shank = pelvis + hip - knee; ankle_dorsiflexion all NaN; source signs). NaN masks must match exactly.
design.exclusions: Every source pair appears once in the ledger. Each pair is classified independently by the task-window rule (D-1 C: exactly one cutPoints interval with a <= start and end <= b). Every rejected pair needs a non-empty reason equal to that classification, and every written pair needs the same task, label and info.
design.receipts: Checks the pilot summary hashes for phase, ledger and source_columns against the files. It checks the base phase hash in both summaries and that the ledger is byte-identical to the base ledger. The code snapshot in the pilot root must match the summary's code_sha256.
design.signs_and_ankle: The pilot is a staging output in source signs. D-UM21-C03-1 rule C (pelvis, knee angle and knee moment x -1) is a downstream transform, and a column that already carries it fails; a test covers this. Ankle alternate-branch frames (|component 2| > 90 deg) and exact (0,0,0) joint-angle triples inside exported windows are reported as flags and do not fail the audit. The D-UM21-C03-2 rule is not applied here.
design.resources: RLIMIT_AS = min(768 MiB, inherited hard limit). It sets single-thread environment variables before imports, plus pa.set_cpu_count(1) and set_io_thread_count(1), and calls nice 19 itself. Each joint dataset has an 8 MiB admission limit. Parquet is streamed in 150-row chunks. A --max-rss-mib self-guard (default 300) stops with exit 4.
design.cli: --source --pilot-root --base-root --subject --condition --output-dir (must not exist; parent must exist), and exactly one of --expected-source-sha256 HEX (job) or --skip-source-hash (bounded probe only; the report sets binding_complete false). Exit 0 pass, 1 check failed, 2 usage/input error, 4 RSS guard.

round2_fixes.R1: New failing check clock_cut_points_aligned_with_joint_frames, with the rule stated in advance in TOLERANCES. For each source HS h, take the mean of that side's HEE and TOE central-difference velocities over frames h+15..h+29; belt speed is the absolute AP component, where AP is the axis with the largest median |window velocity|. Marker frames h+14..h+30 must be finite, not (0,0,0) and not flagged 0. Compare with cvel[h+22+lag-1] for HS within transition intervals (labels a*/d*) +-300 frames, over lags -1000..1000, using the median absolute error. A lag is considered only with at least max(8, ceil(half the lag-0 comparisons)) comparisons. Pass only if |best lag| <= 50 AND err(0) - err(best) <= 0.02 m/s. If not evaluable (no cvel, a missing marker, no transition) the check fails. It is never shifted, never a flag; the cutPoints flag stays informational. Synthetic tests use exact closed forms (a linear belt ramp of 0.001 m/s per frame; a quadratic marker path whose central difference equals the ramp): lag 0 passes; cvel shifted by 150 frames fails with best lag 150 and lag-0 error 0.150; a 40-frame shift fails on the error criterion; a 10-frame shift passes; a missing LTOE fails as not evaluable.
round2_fixes.R2: The job spec bindings now include check_um21_tread_source.py (f340d486...7d87) and source_comparison.json (958a2b2c...ea51), as PM-01 binds them.
round2_fixes.R3: json.dumps(allow_nan=False) runs before open(..., 'x'). On TypeError or ValueError the script writes nothing, prints to stderr and exits 2. Test: a NaN cutPoint reaching clock.cut_points_max gives exit 2 and no audit_report.json.
round2_fixes.R4: Handled, not just noted. finite_difference sets d[i] = NaN wherever values[i] is non-finite, which matches np.gradient's centre term on a near-uniform grid. On the linspace-versus-rational positions: the positions differ only by rounding at non-integer points. A rational position k(n-1)/149 that is not an integer is at least 1/149 from any integer, and when 149 divides k(n-1) linspace's step (n-1)/149 is an exact integer, so the two rules never disagree on whether a sample lands on a source frame. The NaN masks cannot diverge from that cause.

decisions_for_backlog.question: The UMich 2021 treadmill task intervals run on the belt-speed clock, which is 1.7 to 7 seconds off the motion data in some recordings. How should treadmill strides get task labels?

options.label: Exclude recordings that fail the clock check
options.consequence: 5 recordings (AB01 d10, AB01 d5, AB08 i10, AB09 i10, AB10 i0) leave the treadmill release: 916 strides; nothing is estimated. AB01 i5 is held out of every option pending its own decision; its motion is a copy of AB01 i10. If D-UM21-T02-2 is A, AB01 i10 also leaves and this count is 7,408 (154 fewer). Reversible.

options.label: Re-align the measured recordings by their offset
options.consequence: Task intervals of AB01 d10, AB01 d5, AB09 i10 are shifted by the marker-measured offset (229 of 754 decisions change); AB08 i10, AB10 i0 are left out (392 strides). options.label: Keep the source task intervals as published
options.consequence: No change; 229 of 754 stride decisions in AB01 d10, AB01 d5, AB09 i10 stay mislabelled, and AB08 i10, AB10 i0 stay unchecked. decisions_for_backlog.question: In the UMich 2021 treadmill data, participant AB01's 5-degree incline recording is a byte-for-byte copy of the same participant's 10-degree incline recording, except for its task intervals. Which of the two should be released?

options.label: Drop both AB01 i5 and AB01 i10
options.consequence: Neither recording is released (148 + 154 strides left out). Reversible.

options.label: Drop AB01 i5 only
options.consequence: AB01 i5 is left out (148 strides); the motion is released once as AB01 i10 (154 strides). AB01 then has no 5-degree incline recording, and assigning the motion to AB01 i10 rests on the measured slope (9.8-11.0 degrees by three methods) and the marker belt-speed fit (-7 vs -413 frames). Reversible.

options.label: Keep both as published
options.consequence: Both are released; the same motion appears twice, once labelled as a 5-degree incline whose task clock is 4.1 s off it (AB01 i5 then falls under D-UM21-T02-1). Reversible before release.

decisions_for_backlog.why: Every signal and the heel strikes of AB01 i5 equal AB01 i10 byte for byte. The shared motion was walked on a 9.8-11.0 degree slope (midstance foot path, heel-toe pitch and plate force), and only AB01 i10's task clock fits it (-7 vs -413 frames), so the motion belongs to AB01 i10. Releasing both publishes the same strides twice; dropping both discards data whose labels check out.
